content.text:
I submitted **index 69** (Bi 0.07, Cu 0.54, V 0.39) as the best composition. At 6.2e-7 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, about four times either of the others. I don't know how it compares with the best in the library: with 3 measurements across 137 candidates, a better composition could easily be one I never measured.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Region | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.24 / 0.18 / 0.58 | BiVO₄ plus a copper vanadate | 1.6e-7 A |
| 69 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | Close to the copper vanadate Cu₃V₂O₈ | **6.2e-7 A** |
| 78 | 0.10 / 0.78 / 0.12 | Mostly copper oxide | 1.8e-7 A |

- **Why index 69 did best:** my explanation is that copper vanadates absorb 2.4 eV light better than the BiVO₄/V₂O₅-rich films. Moving further toward copper oxide made it worse, as you'd expect, since copper oxide is a poor photoanode. This comes from prior knowledge plus three data points; I didn't check the structure with XRD.
- **Weak model support:** the phase list was too large to return, and I couldn't open the saved copy. So I only got model results for three simple oxides whose IDs I guessed (V₂O₅, CuO, Bi₂O₃). None of the mixed Bi–Cu–V phases were checked, so the required consultations only loosely supported each choice.
- **Last measurement:** index 78 was a deliberate gamble that the trend toward more copper would continue. It didn't pay off. A composition next to index 69 would probably have been the safer choice.
- **Unused budget:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements. XRD matching needs phase IDs that I couldn't get.
